LESSON: WRITING 10.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING: DESCRIPTIVE COMPOSITION (120 -160 WORDS)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words), part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five General.

Key inquiry question: How do we describe things or events? 2. Why is it important to describe things or events clearly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing: Descriptive Composition (120 -160 words) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: Learning independently as learners, individually, writes a descriptive composition.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: Evaluation and decision making skill as learners organise sentences describing how they spent their

leisure time into a paragraph.

92

• Communication and Collaboration: Articulating signs clearly as learners, talk, as they sign, about people or things in the text.

Values:
Integrity: Transparency as learners give feedback to each others work on the compositions proof read.

Link to other subjects:

Learners are able to relate the knowledge of creative writing to their learning in all other subjects.
